# go.generate runs //go:generate directives and tracks `outputs`: a binary
# built from the generated file rebuilds when the directive changes, a
# removed output is generated again, and --clean removes it.
[!exec:go] skip

bit
stdout 'gen ▶ go generate \./gen'
grep 'const Answer = 42' gen/answer.go
exec ./app
stdout '\A42\n\z'

bit
stdout 'gen · no changes'
stdout 'app · no changes'

cp gen.go.changed gen/gen.go
bit
stdout 'gen ▶ go generate \./gen \(''gen/gen\.go'' changed\)'
stdout 'app ▶ go build'
exec ./app
stdout '\A7\n\z'

rm gen/answer.go
bit
stdout 'gen ▶ go generate \./gen \(''gen/answer\.go'' \(removed\) changed\)'
grep 'const Answer = 7' gen/answer.go

bit --clean
! exists gen/answer.go
exists gen/gen.go

-- BUILD.bit --
gen = go.generate {
  package = "./gen"
  outputs = ["gen/answer.go"]
}

app = go.exe {
  package    = "./cmd/app"
  depends_on = [gen]
}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.22
-- gen/gen.go --
package gen

//go:generate sh -c "printf 'package gen\\n\\nconst Answer = 42\\n' > answer.go"
-- gen.go.changed --
package gen

//go:generate sh -c "printf 'package gen\\n\\nconst Answer = 7\\n' > answer.go"
-- cmd/app/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/m/gen"
)

func main() { fmt.Println(gen.Answer) }
